study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dissecting the Heterogeneous Cortical Anatomy of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Normative Models

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression used to estimate vertexwise normative models.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Gaussian process regression (43) was used to estimate separate normative models of CT and SA at each vertex on the cortical surface.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Zabihi2019.pdf.md: Constructing a Normative Model of CT

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Vertexwise cortical thickness and surface area.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Gaussian process regression (43) was used to estimate separate normative models of CT and SA at each vertex on the cortical surface.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Zabihi2019.pdf.md: Constructing a Normative Model of CT

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Primary model uses age and gender; additional confound model includes scanning site, IQ, and FreeSurfer Euler number as covariates.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we generated a developmental model of typical brain development by training a Gaussian process regression model on the TD cohort ( n = 206) using age and gender as covariates (i.e., independent variables) to predict CT (i.e., dependent variable).; we first estimated a normative model for CT additionally including scanning site, IQ and the FreeSurfer Euler number (EN) as covariates.
